newsitem.title: UK: Virgin boss Branson ready for balloon bid.
newsitem.headline: Virgin boss Branson ready for balloon bid.

text.p: British tycoon Richard Branson leaves for Morocco on Friday to prepare for another attempt to be the first to fly around the world by balloon.
A spokeswoman said his trip with two co-pilots was a training weekend and the team would be returning to Britain on Monday to wait for the right weather conditions.
"They'll be waiting here on stand-by in the UK, and as soon as the weather conditions are right they'll go down to Morocco and go," said Mo Foster, spokeswoman for the Virgin Global Challenge.
Branson, the flamboyant 45-year-old boss of the Virgin group of companies, was ready to make the attempt in January this year but it was called off at the last minute due to bad weather.
The spokeswoman said it was difficult to predict when the attempt might take place, but the team was on a three-day alert and checking weather conditions on an hourly basis.
"As soon as we think there might be a possibility we're given about 72 hours to get down to Morocco and get ready to go," Foster said.

As well as attempting the dangerous flight, Mr Branson and his co-pilots, Per Linstrand, who built the prototype balloon, and hang-gliding champion Rory McCarthy, face a race against American balloonist Steve Fossett and a two-man team planning a launch from Switzerland.

"Conditions are developing quite favourably. What you need is a combination of a good, strong jetstream and very strong ground conditions," Foster said. Bad weather on the ground affected their last trip.
Branson and his crew will squeeze into the 10-ft wide capsule for the 32,000 km (20,000 mile) trip, most of which will be spent at an average altitude of 30,000 ft.
If conditions are right the record attempt will start from Marrakesh, Morocco and finish in Oxfordshire, central England.
Branson plans to circumnavigate the globe in 18 days.

Branson's proposed balloon flight would be the latest in a series of record-breaking attempts that have indulged his taste for adventure while earning publicity for his companies, which include Virgin Atlantic Airways, a radio station, a chain of superstores, a cinema chain and ventures in cola and vodka.
Branson and Lindstrand have come close to death twice on previous record-breaking balloon flights in 1987 and 1991.
